title: Apply Index Permutation
statement:
Reorder values according to an index permutation.

Contract
- `values` and `permutation` are non-null arrays with the same length.
- `permutation` contains every index from `0` to `values.length - 1` exactly once.
- Mutate `values` so each original value at index `i` moves to index `permutation[i]`.
- Do not mutate `permutation`.

Examples
- Applying `[2, 0, 1]` to `[10, 20, 30]` changes values to `[20, 30, 10]`.
- Applying `[0, 1, 2]` leaves `[4, 5, 6]` unchanged.
- Applying `[1, 0, 3, 2]` to `[7, 8, 9, 10]` changes values to `[8, 7, 10, 9]`.
hints: Write down where each original index should land before mutating anything.
Cycles explain how an in-place version works, but a temporary copy is also valid for this contract.
For each original index `i`, place its saved value at `permutation[i]`. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(n) extra space.
inputSyntax: Input: values then a semicolon then permutation, for example: [10, 20, 30]; [2, 0, 1]
